## Verdict
REVISE — the design is viable, but reveal lifecycle, filtering/sort integration, and installation cleanup are underspecified in ways that can violate requirements or lose rollback data.

## Critical gaps
- Removing the Agents section also removes its sort/filter header; the plan does not relocate the sort toggle or active `agent_view_label`, including the rule that sorting is disabled while a filtered view is active.
- Federated children must be derived from the aggregate agent projection, not independently from each snapshot; otherwise endpoint agent-view filtering, ordering, and stale semantics can change.
- `pending_agent_reveal` currently uses previous-frame geometry and is consumed before activation succeeds. With a unified tree it must survive zero-height/hidden composition and account for collapsed machine/worktree ancestors, or focus actions can never reveal their target.
- Cleanup and replacement are not transactionally sequenced. Commit verification alone does not ensure clean source, staging may be cross-filesystem, and broad deletion across discovered checkouts can remove rollback data or unrelated files before installation is proven successful.

## Important improvements
- Define the projection’s stable row identity, logical row height/gap, and endpoint-qualified hit target. Explicitly group filtered aggregate agents by workspace while applying priority sorting only within each workspace.
- Make workspace drag targets operate on workspace subtree boundaries and reject agent rows and foreign endpoint subtrees.
- Retire all runtime use of agent-body metrics, agent scrollbar, section-divider hit handling, and agent-scroll resets; retaining the obsolete persisted split field is sufficient for compatibility.
- Build from a disposable clean checkout/worktree at the pinned commit and capture baseline diffs for every checkout before changing artifacts.
- Restrict cleanup to an explicit inventory, avoid symlink ...
